title: Opt into full command-service execution in developer sandboxes
description:
As a Plexus developer, I want to explicitly enable the full command-service execution path in my Amplify sandbox, so that I can test dashboard submission through the real dispatcher, queue, ECS worker, authoritative Task lifecycle, and realtime UI without first merging to staging.

Default sandboxes remain lightweight. The opt-in path must reuse a shared non-production foundation where safe, isolate sandbox application resources and Task/API bindings, use immutable worker images and non-production secrets, preserve active-command replacement safety, and clean up sandbox-owned resources. Production resources and secrets are out of scope.

Feature: Optional sandbox command service

Scenario: Default sandbox remains lightweight
Given a developer creates a sandbox without the command-service opt-in
When the sandbox backend is deployed
Then no command-service ECS application resources are created

Scenario: Opted-in sandbox exercises the integrated path
Given the shared non-production foundation exists
And the developer supplies an explicit sandbox command-service opt-in and immutable worker image
When the sandbox backend is deployed
Then sandbox-specific dispatch and worker application resources use that sandbox Task table and AppSync API
And registered dashboard commands execute through the same Task-authoritative lifecycle used by staging

Scenario: Sandbox isolation fails closed
Given the opt-in configuration references production secrets, an invalid foundation contract, or a mutable image
When deployment is evaluated
Then deployment fails before command-service resources can run with that configuration

Scenario: Sandbox teardown preserves the shared foundation
Given an opted-in sandbox owns command-service application resources
When the sandbox is deleted
Then its queue, dispatcher, worker service, and bindings are removed
And the shared non-production network and image repository remain available
